name: flutter-skeleton
summary: Flutter mobile skeleton (Pub Workspaces + Melos): encapsulated packages and a starter app a new project picks from. The backend is the sibling kotlin-skeleton, the web twin is react-skeleton.

capabilities.summary: Shared lint rules (flutter_lints plus avoid_print and unawaited_futures) every package and app includes.
notFor: Project-specific rules: add them in the app's own analysis_options.yaml

capabilities.summary: One Dio-based REST client for the backend: envelope unwrapping (value, values, pagination), the standard ApiRequestError with its codes, header providers and an error hook. Pure Dart.
notFor: Authentication: tokens and refresh live in auth
Streams (SSE, WebSocket): not here

capabilities.summary: Email and password sign-in, account lifecycle (sign-up, email verification, password reset, account deletion), secure token storage, silent refresh on 401 with a single in-flight refresh, session state (Riverpod), go_router redirect helpers and the forms.
notFor: Magic link, MFA: not built yet
How the screens look: the app owns them (texts are parameters)

capabilities.summary: Legal documents and consents: the sign-up consent boxes, a document page, the re-consent screen and the 403 LEGAL.RECONSENT_REQUIRED handling (go_router redirect to /consent).
notFor: A markdown renderer: documents show as plain selectable text
Cookie banners: not an app concern

capabilities.summary: Board posts, nested comments and reactions: list with paging, detail, editor, idempotent submits, delete and edit only for your own.
notFor: Guest posts, attachments, moderation, search, drafts
Choosing an author profile: the app gives a resolver

capabilities.summary: Push notifications through FCM: device registration, permission prompt, per-kind settings, a test notification, tapped-link handling and removing the device on sign-out. The app initializes Firebase.
notFor: Creating the Firebase project or its config files: the project owns them (google-services.json and GoogleService-Info.plist stay out of git)
Topic or broadcast messages

capabilities.summary: In-app purchase through the App Store and Google Play: the server's product list as the store prices it, buy and restore with the server's account token, every purchase checked by the server before anything opens or finishes, left-over purchases at start, a web checkout address opened in the outside browser (only when the server's channel has the web), and the lookup that tells a person to cancel a store subscription before deleting the account. No screens.
notFor: Creating products or store accounts: the project registers them in App Store Connect and Play Console
Card payment inside the app (WebView): the web checkout opens the outside browser
Refunds, family sharing, offer codes: not built

capabilities.summary: Sign in with a social provider's app SDK token, core only: the provider interface, the nonce, the server call (POST /auth/social/{provider}/token), link and re-authentication tokens for settings, the controller that signs the session in only after the server accepted the token, and which providers to show (GET /auth/methods). The provider SDKs are the social-login-* packages. No screens.
notFor: A provider's SDK: take the social-login-google, -apple, -kakao or -naver package
Browser (code flow) sign-in: that is the web twin
Button looks: the app draws them (each provider has a design guide)

capabilities.summary: Google sign-in for the social login core (google_sign_in 7): returns the ID token for the web client id the server checks.
notFor: Registering the client ids and the package name with SHA-1 in the Google Cloud console: the project does it
Sending a nonce: google_sign_in 7 takes one only once per run

capabilities.summary: Sign in with Apple for the social login core (sign_in_with_apple 8, iOS app only): the ID token with a hashed nonce, the name from the first sign-in, and the token revoke the App Store asks for before an account is deleted.
notFor: Android and web Apple sign-in: a later step (Services ID and callback)
The Sign in with Apple capability and the relay-mail domain: the project registers them with Apple

capabilities.summary: Kakao sign-in for the social login core (kakao_flutter_sdk_user 2): through KakaoTalk when installed, else the Kakao account page; returns the access token.
notFor: KakaoSdk.init and the platform files (URL scheme, Android intent filter): the app does them, the README lists them
The Kakao logo: the repo ships none, see Kakao's design guide

capabilities.summary: Naver sign-in for the social login core (flutter_naver_login 2.1): returns the access token the server checks with Naver's profile API. The Naver SDK puts its client secret in the app.
notFor: A check that the token was issued to this app: Naver offers none we found, the README says what that means
The platform files (meta-data, FlutterFragmentActivity, Nid keys, handleURL): the app does them
The Naver logo: the repo ships none, see Naver's design guide

capabilities.summary: Design tokens as Dart constants, light and dark Material 3 themes that follow the system, and the LoadingView and ErrorView the starter uses.
notFor: A component library: Material widgets are used as they are
A stored theme switch: the theme follows the system

capabilities.summary: The starter app: sign up with consents, verify email, sign in, reset the password, see who you are (GET /auth/me), delete the account, sign out, agree again when a document changes, restore the session on start. It becomes the new project's app.
notFor: Anything beyond sign-in: delete what you do not use, the starter is the minimum

capabilities.summary: The reference app: the starter's flows plus a board tab, a store tab (products, buy, restore, web checkout, my subscription, the cancel-in-the-store notice before account deletion), social sign-in buttons with linking in settings, push settings and a settings tab, wired the way a project would. Read it for wiring; a stamp removes it.
notFor: A base to build on: start from the starter and copy what you need from here
